title: 1997 AHSME Problem 5
statement: A rectangle with perimeter \(176\) is divided into five congruent rectangles as shown in the diagram. What is the perimeter of one of the five congruent rectangles?

solutions.text: Let a small rectangle have sides \(x\) and \(y.\) The common width gives \(3x=2y,\) while the large rectangle has dimensions \(3x\) by \(x+y.\) Its perimeter is \(2(4x+y)=176.\) Since \(y=\frac{3x}{2},\) this is \(11x=176,\) so \(x=16\) and \(y=24.\) One small perimeter is \(2(16+24)=80,\) making C correct.
hints: Let the short and long sides of a small rectangle be \(x\) and \(y\)
The total width is both \(3x\) across the top and \(2y\) across the bottom
